Subject: POC MAP kickoff — activation runway, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC pairing

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to lock a Mutual Action Plan so we can get a sandbox POC running next month. High-level asks from our side:

- Org & tenant setup (invite our SSO service account + service user)
- API key provisioning for staging (ephemeral keys preferred)
- IP allowlist for inbound requests and webhook callbacks
- VPC peering for secure model calls and KV cache traffic

Can you confirm the earliest dates you can:
1) create the OrbitMed org and invite two admin users
2) issue staging API keys (short-lived)
3) accept VPC peering (we can schedule maintenance windows)

We also have a short security checklist our InfoSec needs (SOC2 pointers, data retention settings). I'll attach the initial MAP template we filled on our side.

Goal: have a functioning POC environment and initial quality run by 2026-09-10. If that window is tight, tell us which milestones we can compress.

Thanks —
Sam Walker
Director of Integrations | OrbitMed
sam@orbitmed.com
+1 415 555 0218

Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a proposed Mutual Action Plan (compact) that maps owners and target dates. I've attached our MAP spreadsheet (redwood-map-v1.xlsx) with the same entries so we can iterate in a single doc. Please confirm and we'll lock the kickoff call.

Proposed MAP (owners / targets):
- Org & tenant setup: Redwood to create OrbitMed org + invite 2 admins — owner: karthik_iyer — target: 2026-08-20
- Staging API keys (ephemeral): Redwood to provision ephemeral staging keys + sample SDK usage — owner: marissa_cole — target: 2026-08-24
- IP allowlist: OrbitMed to provide CIDRs, Redwood to confirm and apply — owner: neha_kapoor (Redwood) / Sam (OrbitMed) — target: 2026-08-25 (apply)
- VPC peering: network exchange, routing verification, smoke test — owner: priyom_das — target peer window: 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-03 (staging smoke on 09-04)
- Security onboarding checkpoint: share SOC2 summary + retention settings — owner: karthik_iyer — target: 2026-08-26

If any of the target windows are infeasible for you, tell us which items to prioritize (we can fast-track API keys and IP allowlist and hold peering as the last step).

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.xlsx (MAP + milestone tracker)

Next steps:
1) confirm owners and the single-sheet MAP by EOD 2026-08-19
2) schedule a 30-min kickoff with network and security folks

I'll loop in Marissa (CS) to provision the keys and Priyom for networking.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Sam / team —

Quick technical constraints and confirmations from the infra side before we lock dates: 

- VPC peering: we prefer a 2-hour maintenance window for the BGP route propagation checks. Suggested peer window: 2026-09-01 02:00–08:00 UTC (low traffic).
- Required customer egress CIDR (for peering acceptance): we need a /16 or /20 range; example: 10.84.0.0/16 (please confirm final CIDR).
- Firewall & IP allowlist: for webhook callbacks our outbound IPs will be in the 34.120.0.0/14 range; we'll provide a signed allowlist CSV (poa-ip-allowlist.csv).
- API keys: we support ephemeral keys (TTL 24h) for early staging. For longer tests we can generate time-bound tokens (7d). Keys are scoped by org and by route; we'll publish a sample scope manifest in the MAP doc.

I'll attach a simple VPC peering diagram (vpc-peering-diagram.png) and the allowlist CSV to make it easier for your network team.

Notes: once peering is established we run a KV-cache smoke test and a 30-min load replay (controlled QPS) before handing to your QA. That smoke is the gating step for the formal sign-off.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Network & Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
